items.title: Herb Morand Interview, 1950-03-12
items.q: So I left in 41 and came home and start playing with George Lewis. I worked with George Lewis a long time. George Lewis's jazz band.

ctx.x: When did you leave Chicago, Herb? You mean to come back to New York?

Yeah. Well, I left when this country declared war. So I hadn't been home in 13 years at that time. My mother and father was living, so I decided to come home. I thought maybe I would be drafted, but I missed the draft by a couple of years. So I had a nice job playing on the north side in the nightclub. So I turned the job over to P.C. William, my drummer. And the proprietor of the place liked me so much, I just, I couldn't tell him I was leaving. I just left. I didn't tell him anything. I hate to do that, but I'd…
Around that time, didn't you get an offer from Sidney Boucher to join him in Boston? A few years after that, at least.

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1958-11-14
items.q: No, that's not Herb Moran's brother. That's another McGee.

ctx.x: Now McGee, is that, that's Herb Moran?

No, that's not Herb Moran's brother. That's another McGee. That's another McGee. Yeah, he lives in Oakland right now. He was one of the last time I saw him. He quit playing. Used to wear a derby all the time. And then after Boyd's left there, that's where the D came in there. That's where him and Billy got acquainted and got married for. I stood for the wait.
That was all in the 30s then? That was in the 30s.

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-10-12
items.q: Did, um, Herb Moran play with you at Madison? Oh, he played with me there in the town space sometimes.

ctx.x: So, okay, can you remember the time when you were playing with Ivan Thomas, when he was murdered? Yeah, sure. Can you tell us something about that? One thing I'd like to know is, can you remember any of the other people in the band? Yeah. Pomp. Pomp. Changer. Bruce Robinson, the piano. Walter Preston playing banjo. Chani on the drum. Steve Antonis. Uh-huh. And a young footballer named Al was playing tennis. Uh-huh. Those old boys were in that band at that time. He didn't have a bass player? No, he was using two…

School. I have a kid. Nick's symphony. His father had a grocery store. About stuff like stuff That's how I got to find it with Nick. He liked it so much, so... He liked to run a business, and he really runs a business really good. I'd better complain about Nick, but he still runs my business, right? He does not? He's alright. I mean, he's not in music. No, he's alive. He's alive. Yeah. Um, can you remember how long he was your manager, and when Dorothy Tate took over? Can you remember, I've never been able to…

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1960-01-25
items.q: Well, after Talbot died, we had Moran.

ctx.x: It was a change in proposition. Before I got here, Moran was there.
Well, after Talbot died, we had Moran.

Yeah, that's right. Yeah, that's right. But I've been, even before that Moran was there, somebody told me. I don't know. I'll take it back. I'm not sure about that. That was before I got here, you know, and people tell you things. Yeah, I don't remember.
